heading: INT. FAMILY FUNERAL HOME - VIEWING ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. FAMILY FUNERAL HOME - VIEWING ROOM - DAY
Gray carpet, a bank of white lilies, a closed walnut casket at the far wall.
Folding chairs in three rows.
A tissue box on every sixth chair.
The air conditioning hums like an apology.
MARGARET "MAGGIE" DELACROIX-OWUSU (50s, black dress, hair pinned tight) stands at the casket, one hand flat on the lid.
She does not speak.
Her sister, JOSEPHINE "JOJO" DELACROIX-KRAMER (40s, same dress, cheaper shoes) hovers three feet behind with a clutch purse she keeps opening and closing.
On the front row, their elderly aunt, BEATRIX FAIRCHILD-ANYANWU (80s, hat with a small black veil) knits something shapeless.
Beside her, her grandson, NATHANIEL "NATE" OYELOWO-FAIRCHILD (20s, tie too short, a phone he keeps checking and pocketing) sits stiffly.
She straightens the lilies.
She straightens them again.
The other one stands behind her and watches her do it, purse snapping shut.
Maggie turns.
Looks past Jojo, at the door.
Jojo follows her eyes.
No one there.
Beatrix's needles click.
Nate checks his phone.
Puts it away.
Checks it.
Maggie crosses to the front row and sits, one chair apart from Beatrix.
She smooths her skirt.
Jojo remains standing.
After a long moment, she sits too, on the other side of her, so that she is flanked by her sister and her aunt.
Maggie reaches over without looking and takes Jojo's hand.
Jojo squeezes once.
Neither lets go.
Beatrix's needles stop.
She lays them in her lap.
At the back of the room, the door swings open on its own and settles.
The four of them turn at the same time.
